# Cris Santos Company | Manufacturing | Enterprise: Global medical device maker

> Cris Santos Company, Inc. is a publicly traded enterprise with 12,000 employees, operating as a connected medical device manufacturer (electromedical equipment).

This folder is a self-contained scenario. Read this page first, then open the project folders in step order (step-01 to step-10). Each project folder has a `_context.md` explaining what that deliverable looks like for this company.

## At a glance
| | |
|---|---|
| Legal name | Cris Santos Company, Inc. |
| Legal form | Publicly traded corporation (SEC registrant) |
| Ownership | Public shareholders; board with audit and risk committees |
| Employees | 12,000 employees |
| Annual receipts (fictional) | $4.8 billion |
| Size tier | Enterprise: Single-sector business with 1,000 or more employees |
| SBA size status | Not small (SBA standard for NAICS 334510: 1,250 employees; 13 CFR 121.201) |
| Primary industry | NAICS 334510 Electromedical and Electrotherapeutic Apparatus Manufacturing |
| Vertical | Manufacturing (NAICS sector 31-33) |
| Primary system | Device software development and manufacturing systems (PLM and MES) |
| IT footprint | Large hybrid estate: multiple clouds, data centers, OT where relevant, hundreds of applications |
| Who owns security and compliance | CISO, dedicated GRC team, internal audit, three lines model |

## What the business handles
- **Sensitive data:** Device design files and source code; SBOMs and vulnerability data; export-controlled technical data (EAR/ITAR where applicable); patient data received from devices in service (may be PHI when handled for a covered entity)
- **Critical systems:** MES; ERP / PLM; DCS / PLCs / robotics; SCADA and historians; Quality/LIMS; CAD/CAM and CNC networks

## Who regulates it
Department of Defense (DFARS/CMMC, DCSA); Department of State DDTC (ITAR); Department of Commerce BIS (EAR, ICTS); FDA (medical device cybersecurity, food facilities); CISA (Chemical & Critical Manufacturing SRMA)

| Requirement | Citation | Size thresholds / exemptions |
|---|---|---|
| [DFARS 252.204-7012 Safeguarding Covered Defense Information and Cyber Incident Reporting](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/section-252.204-7012) | 48 CFR 252.204-7012 (MAY 2024) | No small-business exemption; flowdown required to subcontracts involving CDI/operationally critical support, including commercial products/services. |
| [CMMC Program rule (32 CFR Part 170) + DFARS CMMC acquisition rule (DFARS 252.204-7021)](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/09/10/2025-17359/defense-federal-acquisition-regulation-supplement-assessing-contractor-implementation-of) | 32 CFR Part 170 (FR Doc. 2024-22905, Oct. 15, 2024); 48 CFR 204.75 and 252.204-7021 (NOV 2025) (FR Doc. 2025-17359, Sep. 10, 2025, DFARS Case 2019-D041) | No size exemption. Applies to solicitations/contracts above the micro-purchase threshold, except those exclusively for COTS items (32 CFR 170.3(c)). Level set by DoD per contract (FCI -> L1; CUI -> L2; high-priority CUI -> L3). Conditional status valid 180 days; final L1 1 year, L2/L3 3 years. |
| [ITAR (International Traffic in Arms Regulations)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-22/chapter-I/subchapter-M) | 22 CFR Parts 120-130 (registration 22 CFR 122.1; encrypted-data carve-out 22 CFR 120.54(a)(5)) | No size threshold; one occasion of manufacturing/exporting triggers registration. |
| [EAR (Export Administration Regulations)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-15/subtitle-B/chapter-VII/subchapter-C) | 15 CFR Parts 730-774 (encrypted-data carve-out 15 CFR 734.18(a)(5)) | No size threshold. |
| [FD&C Act sec. 524B cyber device requirements](https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title21-section360n-2&num=0&edition=prelim) | 21 U.S.C. 360n-2 | None. |

Whether each requirement applies at this size is decided at the start of P03, the gap analysis (build step 5).

## The 10 projects for this company, in build order

| 1 | [P05 Business Impact Analysis (BIA)](step-01_P05_business-impact-analysis/_context.md) | Enterprise-wide BIA. Quantified impact; dependency mapping; third parties. | Company facts only |
| 2 | [P02 System Security Plan (SSP)](step-02_P02_system-security-plan/_context.md) | A high-value system (Moderate or High impact). Full SSP; common control provider inheritance. System: Device software development and manufacturing systems (PLM and MES). | P05: which systems matter and how long they can be down |
| 3 | [P04 Control-to-Cloud Architecture Mapping](step-03_P04_cloud-control-mapping/_context.md) | Multi-cloud enterprise architecture. Platform; landing zone; workload; SaaS layers; common controls. | P02: the system boundary and its controls |
| 4 | [P01 Risk Register](step-04_P01_risk-register/_context.md) | Enterprise risk register integrated with ERM. 60+ risks; aggregation to enterprise risk (NIST IR 8286). | P05 impact levels; P02 and P04 systems and controls |
| 5 | [P03 Regulatory Gap Analysis](step-05_P03_regulatory-gap-analysis/_context.md) | All applicable regulations across the enterprise. Requirement-level; evidence sampling; regulator-ready. Regulation: FD&C Act section 524B (cyber devices). | P01 risks; P02 control statements |
| 6 | [P06 Security Policy Set](step-06_P06_security-policies/_context.md) | 5 policies within a policy hierarchy. Policies; standards; procedures; exceptions process. | P03 gaps; P01 risks |
| 7 | [P07 Security Control Assessment](step-07_P07_control-assessment/_context.md) | 40+ controls. Formal assessment; statistical sampling; independence. | P02 control statements; P06 policies |
| 8 | [P08 Incident Response Runbook](step-08_P08_incident-response-runbook/_context.md) | Incident type with SEC materiality assessment step. Runbooks integrated with crisis; legal; disclosure committee. Incident: Exploited vulnerability in a fielded connected medical device. | P05 recovery order; P01 risks; P03 notification duties |
| 9 | [P09 SOC 2 Readiness Checklist](step-09_P09_soc2-readiness/_context.md) | All categories; multiple service lines. Readiness for Type 2 across service lines. | Evidence from P02, P06 and P07 |

## How to use this page in a meeting
1. Read **At a glance** aloud. It sets who the company is and how big it is.
2. Walk through **Who regulates it**. It explains why the projects exist.
3. Open one project folder and its `_context.md`, then the working files next to it.
